## What does instant coffee jar mean for an Indian kitchen? For most of us, that jar on the counter is more than just a grocery item; it is the fuel for our 7 AM hustle or the excuse for a mid-day break. But here is the thing: not every cup is created equal. If you love a thick, creamy milk coffee that doesn't break the bank, the Ultra Blend (70% coffee, 30% chicory) at ₹209 for 50g is a reliable daily driver. However, if you are chasing that sharp, clean hit of caffeine to wake up your brain, switching to a pure coffee option from Purity Beans changes everything. Try this: brew your coffee with slightly less hot water than usual to keep the flavor concentrated before adding milk. For those who want a gourmet experience, the freeze-dried Purica Arabica at ₹329 for 50g offers a smooth, chocolatey finish that feels like a cafe treat right in your own kitchen.

### A plain definition

Whatever brought you here, the label settles it. The other single jars on this page are 0% chicory.

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar? Most of us just grab whatever is on the shelf, but the real secret is in the fine print. When you look at a label, if you see 'coffee' listed after 'chicory' or 'additives,' you're likely drinking a filler-heavy blend. It's a simple habit: flip the jar and check the percentage.
